author: Benjamin George Sports Editor
title: South Harrison sweeps tri-match vs. Doddridge County and Lincoln, Bulldogs split | West Virginia High School Sports | wvnews.com
text:
LOST CREEK, W.Va. - South Harrison volleyball looked in well-oiled condition Thursday night, defeating both Doddridge County and Lincoln in straight sets, improving the Hawks to 22-5-1 as the regular season nears its conclusion.
Between the Bulldogs and Cougars, Doddridge County would earn a hard-fought victory in straight sets to collect its ninth win and move to 9-17, while the Cougars would finish the night 0-2 and fall to 11-13 on the year.
The Hawks defeated Doddridge County 25-15, 25-19, while Doddridge County defeated Lincoln 25-23, 25-20. South Harrison defeated Lincoln 25-15, 25-19.
South Harrison-Doddridge County
The first set saw South Harrison jump in front, holding a 12-6 lead at the first timeout. The Hawks continue to roll afterwards to securely take the set 25-15.
Set two saw the Bulldogs find footing early, with two aces by Kamryn Satterfield opening the set with a 4-3 lead. After trading blows back and forth, the first timeout found the Hawks with a 10-9 advantage.
Following the breather, South Harrison would hit its stride and rip off a 9-3 run to position themselves at a 19-12 cushion. This run would end up being key to handling any comeback effort from the Bulldogs, with the Hawks locking down the 25-19 second set win to secure the victory.
Hawks senior Delainey Lowther recorded 10 total points along with 13 assists for the double-double. Sophomore Audrey Burnside also had a high-quality performance with 11 assists, 9 kills and 2 aces, while Gabby Davis put down a team-leading 4 aces and 5 kills.
For the Bulldogs, Satterfield reached a major milestone, recording assist No. 1,000 in her high school career. Junior Brooke DeHaven was everywhere with 5 kills, 3 blocks and 5 digs throughout the match.
Doddridge County-Lincoln
Thursday's second round of game action was a roller coaster of emotions for Bulldogs fans.
The Cougars opened up the first set with a 6-0 run, prompting head coach Wesley Ezell to take a timeout. After the break, Doddridge County put up five unanswered before losing its stride and seeing the rally hopes dwindle as Lincoln upped its advantage to 9, and Ezell would take his second timeout with the score 17-8 Cougars.
Doddridge County then pieced together a remarkable rally, rattling off a 10-3 run to move the score to 20-18 Lincoln. After another timeout, the squads would trade back and forth, with the Bulldogs taking a 22-21 lead and not losing it again, coming out victorious 25-23.
Set two was a back-and-forth affair to start. Cougars junior Aundrea Rockwell made her presence known with consecutive aces to put Lincoln up 5-3 early on. However, the Bulldogs would retie the set at 5 soon after and not find themselves coming from behind again.
After another tie at 9-9, Doddridge County put down a 6-2 run, with an ace from Evalynn Rial sending the set into its first break.
The Cougars would push back in a strong fashion, whittling the deficit to as low as one, and sending the game into its second break via a Doddridge County timeout at 18-17 Bulldogs.
Ezell's sense of timeout calls seemed to have been otherworldly Thursday night, as the Bulldogs would push through and end on a 7-3 run to secure both the set and match.
Coach Ezell said postgame, "That first set, they took the momentum and went with it. We had to fall and find our way back into it, but once we did, the momentum started to switch and we did all the right things.
"They just kept fighting and fighting and believing they could at least be in the game."
South Harrison-Lincoln
The night's final round saw the Hawks trailing 4-2 to begin, heavily aided by 2 blocks from Rockwell. South Harrison regained the lead 5-4, but the Cougars would hop back in front with help from an ace by Arianna Finch.
However, this would be the last lead Lincoln would be able to take in the first set, as an ace by the Hawks' Kennedy Southern would propel them into a 7-6 lead they would not relinquish.
They would tear off on a 14-3 run, strongly enhanced by 2 straight aces from Amelia Critchfield and another ace from Davis to wrap up set one.
Set two saw the Hawks overcome a deficit once again as Lincoln jumped out to a 3-0 advantage. In no time it seemed, the Hawks had erased the deficit and extended the advantage to 11-3, with major help coming from Davis firing out 3 of her 4 aces in this span.
The Cougars would not quit, however, putting down a run of their own and carving the lead to as low as two. In the end, the deficit would prove too great to conquer, as the Hawks finished the game with 3 consecutive points to put away the Cougars 25-19 in the second set and secure the sweep for the night.
Head coach Breanna Sears spoke highly of her squad's efforts. "We prepared them and talked about what we needed to do, and I felt they executed that plan pretty well," said Sears.
"I was really proud of their performance and what they did. It always gets nerve-wracking this time of year as a coach, knowing what's coming up in the postseason. To watch them play against a regional team you might see again and seeing how they reacted and played was really encouraging."
The Hawks will next be in action Oct. 14 for a home tri-match against Petersburg and Berkeley Springs.
Doddridge County's next match will be a home contest on Oct. 13 against visiting St. Mary's. Finally, the Cougars' next game will be a road trip to Tucker County on Oct. 12.
